run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Querying Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' returned 1800 indices. Their document counts fall into exactly two groups: 5 indices hold 500 documents each and the remaining 1795 hold 1 document each. Because the five largest are tied at 500 documents, the top 5 by document count are those five indices: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20, app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15, all reporting health green with store sizes between 46.7kb and 47.9kb. No sixth index exceeds 1 document, and the tie means any ordering within the five is arbitrary.

claims.text: The largest indices under 'app-184-*' each hold 500 documents: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (500 docs, 47.8kb, green), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500 docs, 46.9kb, green), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500 docs, 47.9kb, green), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500 docs, 46.9kb, green) and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500 docs, 46.7kb, green); the next entries in that ordering hold only 1 document.

A numeric-descending sort of docs.count over all 'app-184-*' indices returns exactly those five 500-document indices first, followed by indices with docs.count 1, for example app-184-security-worker-2024.01.36.

Grouping the 1800 'app-184-*' indices by document count yields only two groups: 5 indices with docs.count 500 and 1795 indices with docs.count 1, so the five largest are tied at 500 and no other matched index exceeds 1 document.

The read-back slice of the full index listing was truncated (10 of 1800 rows returned), so the per-index rows beyond those shown here are not individually quoted; the grouped and sorted views cover all 1800 indices in aggregate.

The five largest indices are exactly tied at 500 documents, so a strict 1-to-5 ranking among them cannot be established from document count alone.
next_steps: If a strict ordering among the five tied 500-document indices is needed, compare store.size or primary store size instead of document count (app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 at 47.9kb is the largest by size in the observed rows).
